PSD support requires vectorization convention. diffcp uses SCS convention: lower-triangular column-major, -diagonals scaled 2\sqrt{2}. package exports vec_symm() unvec_symm() round-trips symmetric matrices packed vector form. trace-coefficient row equality constraint sparse — diagonal entries contribute, build explicitly: X trace 1 (solver tolerance) PSD (smallest eigenvalue ≥−10−9\ge -10^{-9}). code: DIM <- 5L n   <- DIM * (DIM + 1L) %/% 2L          # 15  trace_row <- numeric(n) pos <- 1L for (col in seq_len(DIM)) {   trace_row[pos] <- 1.0   pos <- pos + (DIM - col + 1L)         # next diagonal in column-major lower-tri }  A <- rbind(   Matrix(matrix(trace_row, nrow = 1L), sparse = TRUE),   -Diagonal(n)) A <- as(A, "CsparseMatrix") b <- c(1.0, numeric(n))  C <- matrix(0, DIM, DIM) C[1, 1] <- 1; C[DIM, DIM] <- -1 c_vec <- vec_symm(C)  cone_dict <- list(z = 1L, s = DIM)  res <- solve_only(A, b, c_vec, cone_dict,                   tol_gap_abs = 1e-10,                   tol_gap_rel = 1e-10,                   tol_feas    = 1e-10) X <- unvec_symm(res$x, DIM) sum(diag(X)) #> [1] 1 range(eigen(X, symmetric = TRUE, only.values = TRUE)$values) #> [1] -2.080584e-12  1.000000e+00

text: canonical use case: shadow prices. Take small LP — profit-maximizing production plan labor materials budget — ask, given optimum, much profit change per extra unit labor? number dual variable labor constraint. diffcp lets compute sensitivity perturbation data, including ones closed-form dual interpretation. solve maxx1,x2≥03x1+5x2s.t.2x1+x2≤100,x1+3x2≤90, \max_{x_1, x_2 \ge 0}\; 3 x_1 + 5 x_2 \quad \text{s.t.}\quad 2 x_1 + x_2 \le 100,\; x_1 + 3 x_2 \le 90, ask: optimum respond small change labor-budget right-hand side, b1=100b_1 = 100? rewrite maximization minimization −c⊤x-c^\top x, encode two budget inequalities two non-negativity inequalities four rows non-negative orthant slack constraint: optimum makes x1=42x_1 = 42, x2=16x_2 = 16, profit =206= 206. Now use D ask optimal xx change got one extra unit labor (Δb1=1\Delta b_1 = 1): d$dx says extra unit labor increases x1x_1 0.6 decreases x2x_2 0.2, corresponding profit change 0.80.8 per unit labor: labor-budget shadow price, recovered D rather dual variable yy. advantage going D instead dual: generalizes. can ask question non-trivial perturbations AA (productivity gain particular input), c (price change particular product), combination. dual variable answers canonical RHS-perturbation question; D answers single call. DT answers opposite question. Suppose downstream loss L(x*)L(x^\ast) — say, smooth function optimum known gradient ∂L/∂x*\partial L / \partial x^\ast. adjoint computes gradient LL respect every data entry (,b,c)(, b, c) one shot: training loop ’d feed da$db da$dc straight parameter update.
code: A_lp <- sparseMatrix(i = c(1, 2, 3,  1, 2, 4),                      j = c(1, 1, 1,  2, 2, 2),                      x = c(2, 1, -1, 1, 3, -1),                      dims = c(4, 2)) b_lp <- c(100, 90, 0, 0) c_lp <- c(-3, -5) cones_lp <- list(l = 4L)  res <- solve_and_derivative(A_lp, b_lp, c_lp, cones_lp, mode = "dense",                             tol_gap_abs = 1e-10, tol_gap_rel = 1e-10,                             tol_feas    = 1e-10) res$x      # optimal production plan #> [1] 42 16 -sum(c_lp * res$x)   # max profit #> [1] 206 dA <- sparseMatrix(i = integer(0), j = integer(0), x = numeric(0),                    dims = c(4, 2)) db <- c(1, 0, 0, 0) dc <- numeric(2) d  <- res$D(dA, db, dc) d$dx                       # change in optimal production #> [1]  0.6 -0.2 -sum(c_lp * d$dx)          # change in profit #> [1] 0.8 ## Suppose dL/dx* is given (e.g. from autodiff in a larger model). dL_dx <- c(1.0, -0.5) dL_dy <- numeric(length(res$y)) dL_ds <- numeric(length(res$s)) da    <- res$DT(dL_dx, dL_dy, dL_ds) da$db                 # gradient of L w.r.t. each entry of b #> [1]  7.000000e-01 -4.000000e-01 -6.162041e-12 -2.615861e-12 da$dc                 # gradient of L w.r.t. each entry of c #> [1] 3.130900e-10 1.741567e-10

what: Forward versus adjoint: when to use each
title: Differentiating Through a Cone Program with diffcp
text: D DT access underlying Jacobian, cost profile differs: D(dA, db, dc) right-multiplication Jacobian. Cost one solve linear system per call. Use D small number perturbation directions (e.g., parameter sweeps) want forecast effect optimum. DT(dx, dy, ds) right-multiplication Jacobian’s transpose. per-call cost, answer gradient respect data entries simultaneously. Use DT upstream gradient optimum (typically autodiff system) need propagate conic optimization. mode = "dense" factors M first call amortizes cost across subsequent D / DT invocations problem, right choice ’ll evaluate either operator many times.

title: Differentiating Through a Cone Program with diffcp
text: solve_and_derivative accepts two modes inner linear-algebra step: mode = "lsqr" (default): matrix-free conjugate-gradient- style iterative solve M operator. Memory O(nnz())O(\text{nnz}()); iteration count grows conditioning MM. Appropriate large sparse problems. mode = "dense": build MM dense matrix, factor Eigen’s LDLT, reuse factorization across D / DT calls. Cost O(N3)O(N^3) , O(N2)O(N^2) per call, N=m+n+1N = m + n + 1. Appropriate small problems workflows re-apply D / DT many times. modes produce answer within solver tolerance. dense path matches Python’s (M⊤M).ldlt().solve(M⊤⋅rhs)(M^\top M).\mathrm{ldlt}().\mathrm{solve}(M^\top \cdot \mathrm{rhs}) bit--bit; LSQR path agrees dense path roughly 10−610^{-6} default atol = btol = 1e-8.

title: diffcp 0.1.0
text: solve_only(, b, c, cone_dict, ...) — forward solve convex cone program via Clarabel (default) SCS, supporting six standard cones (zero, nonneg, SOC, PSD, exponential, exponential dual). Quadratic objectives via P argument supported forward-mode (mirroring Python diffcp). solve_and_derivative(, b, c, cone_dict, mode, ...) — solves cone program returns optimal (x, y, s) together two callables D(dA, db, dc) DT(dx, dy, ds) apply derivative adjoint supplied perturbations. mode = "lsqr" (default): matrix-free LSQR via M operator. mode = "dense": dense M matrix factored Eigen LDLT. pi(x, cones, dual) — projection onto Cartesian product cones, dual = TRUE selecting dual product cone. PSD-cone forward solves Clarabel automatically permute rows entries b SCS lower-triangular ordering Clarabel upper-triangular ordering, permute y / s back return.

title: diffcp 0.1.0
text: numerical core faithful port C++ source cvxgrp/diffcp (linop.cpp, cones.cpp, deriv.cpp, lsqr.cpp), called R via RcppEigen. R file annotated ## DIFFCP SOURCE: <upstream path> pointing corresponding lines upstream Python source.

title: diffcp 0.1.0
text: 676 tests, faithful ports every -scope test tests/test_clarabel.py, tests/test_clarabel_psd.py, tests/test_scs.py, tests/test_cone_prog_diff.py upstream Python repository. Test fixtures pinned Python diffcp’s outputs atol bounds Python uses (1e-8 finite-difference D-vs-FD agreement; 1e-4 SCS-vs-Clarabel cross-checks; 1e-12 round-trips).

title: diffcp 0.1.0
text: lpgd / lpgd_left / lpgd_right derivative modes (used cvxpylayers QP degenerate-derivative cases). Batch parallel APIs (solve_and_derivative_batch, solve_only_batch). lsmr mode. ECOS solver branch (ECOS unmaintained).
